This Writ Petition Is Filed Under Articles 226
And 227 Of The Constitution Of India Read With
Section 482 Of Cr.P.C., Praying To Quash The Entire
Criminal Proceedings In C.C.No. 20381/ 2021 On The
File Of V Addl. Chief Metropolitan Magistrate At
Bengaluru, Pending Against The Petitioner For The
Alleged Offences U/S. 419, 467, 468, 471, 420 And 204 Of
Ipc As Abuse Of Process Of Law And Also Violative Of
Article 21 Of The Constitution Of India, Vide
Annexure-D.
 This Writ Petition, Coming On For Preliminary
Hearing In 'B' Group, This Day, The Court Made The
Following:
 Order

The petitioner is before this Court calling in question proceedings in C.C.No.20381/2021, pending before the V Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Bengaluru, for the offences under Sections 419, 467, 468, 471, 420 and 204 of the IPC.

2. Heard Sri H.N.Venkatesh, learned counsel for petitioner Sri Mahesh Shetty, learned High Court Government Pleader for respondent No.1 and Sri B.M.Arun, learned counsel for respondent No.2.
NC: 2023:KHC:21390 3.

Facts in brief germane, are as follows:
The petitioner is accused No.1 in the aforesaid proceedings.
Respondent No.2 is the complainant.

The allegation made in the complaint is that, the petitioner challenged the mutation entries in respect of the properties in Survey Nos.8/2A1, 16/3, 21/1A,
30/4C, 58/1A1A, 60/2C, 61/1C, 62/1C and 90/1 of Hulimavu village on the strength of a Will dated 05.01.1976 and also on the basis of their right under succession.
The respondent No.2 herein objected the mutation proceedings.
The Assistant Commissioner upheld the claim of the petitioner / accused No.1 and deleted the initial entries standing in the name of the great grandfather of respondent No.2.

In the said proceedings petitioner No.1 having put forward an unregistered Will,

sentences.text: 2 respondent No.2 filed the above complaint alleging that the said Will was concocted and fabricated by forging the signature of the testator.
On the registration of the crime, the petitioner along with other accused had knocked at the doors of this Court in Crl.P.No.6464/2016.

A co-ordinate Bench of this Court entertaining the petition,
quashed the proceedings against NC: 2023:KHC:21390 accused Nos.2 to 5 and directed that the investigation would continue against the petitioner - accused No.1,
who was the first petitioner in the aforesaid case.
The police after continuation of the investigation have filed their charge sheet.
The filing of the charge sheet is what drives the petitioner yet again to this Court, in the subject petition.

4. Learned counsel for the petitioner would contend with vehemence that the private complaint was filed without appending an affidavit, which is essential in terms of the law laid down by the Apex Court in the case of PRIYANKA SRIVASTAVA VS. STATE OF UTTAR PRADESH AND OTHERS reported in (2015) 6 SCC 287, which is followed subsequently in the case of BABU VENKATESH AND OTHERS Vs. STATE OF KARNATAKA AND ANOTHER reported in (2022) SCC Online SC 200.

sentences.text: He would further contend that the matter which is purely civil in nature has sought to be given a colour of crime.
The complainant has no locus even to claim the properties from the hands let alone on the allegation of forgery.

He would seek quashment of the entire proceedings, NC:
2023:KHC:21390 contending that further proceedings if permitted to continue, it would become an abuse of the process of law.

5. On the other hand, Sri B.M.Arun, learned counsel for respondent No.2 taking this Court to the documents appended to the petition would contend that the co-ordinate Bench of this Court in Crl.P.No.6464/2016 disposed on 31.01.2019, observing that the petitioner was prima facie guilty of forgery, rejected the petition only insofar as accused No.1 - the petitioner is concerned, and that order has become final.
The police after investigation, have filed their charge sheet.
The charge sheet clearly points at the petitioner qua the allegations, prima facie.

Therefore, it is a matter of trial for the petitioner to come out clean and he would seek dismissal of the petition.
6. Learned High Court Government Pleader would toe the lines of the learned counsel for respondent No.2, who seek dismissal of the petition as the allegations would require a trial and the charge sheet is already filed by the police.
I have given my anxious consideration to the submissions made by the learned counsel for both the parties and have perused the material on record.
8. The afore-narrated facts are not in dispute.
Respondent No.2 is the complainant, who seeks to register a private complaint in P.C.R.No.8250/2016.

The private complaint comes to be registered on 05.08.2016 without it being accompanied by an affidavit, as required in terms of the law laid down in the case of PRIYANKA SRIVASTAVA VS. STATE OF UTTAR PRADESH AND OTHERS Smt Savithramma vs State Of Karnataka on 20 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/177768181/
3 reported in (2015) 6 SCC 287.

entities.text: PRIYANKA SRIVASTAVA VS. STATE OF UTTAR PRADESH AND OTHERS Smt Savithramma vs State Of Karnataka
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Apex Court had directed that complaint which is not accompanied by an affidavit should not be entertained by the learned Magistrate.
The said judgment is further reiterated by the Apex Court in the case of BABU VENKATESH AND OTHERS Vs. STATE OF KARNATAKA AND ANOTHER reported in (2022) SCC Online SC 200.

entities.text: BABU VENKATESH AND OTHERS Vs. STATE OF KARNATAKA AND ANOTHER reported in (2022) SCC Online SC 200
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The law as laid down by the Apex Court then, is applicable to every circumstance is also not in dispute.
Those judgments would not be applicable to the case at hand, as the petitioner was already before the co-ordinate Bench in Crl.P.No.6464/2016.
The petitioner challenged the registration of a crime in Crime No.520/2016 in the year 2016 itself.
This Court dismisses the petition insofar as this petitioner - accused No.1 is concerned.

The co-ordinate Bench has observed as follows:
8.
In the complaint, specific allegations are made against petitioner No.1 that the Will in question is fabricated and the signature of K.M. Muniramaiah is forged.
It is also alleged that the Will is bogus, concocted and fabricated with forged signatures.
These allegations on the face of it attract the ingredients of the offences punishable under Sections 120-B, 465, 468, 420 and 471 of I.P.C.
Therefore, the argument of the learned counsel for the petitioners that the allegations made against the petitioners are purely civil in nature, cannot be accepted.
9. It is also relevant to note that the Will put forward by the petitioners is an unregistered document.
It has seen the light of the day nearly 40 years after the date of the alleged execution which itself gives rise to suspicion surrounding its execution.

Though the learned counsel for the petitioners has put forth a contention that the respondent has no locus standi to initiate criminal proceedings, yet the facts discussed above, clearly indicate that the revenue entries stood in the name of the forefathers of respondent No.2 and the same were sought to be challenged by petitioner No.1 on the basis of the Will.

Further it is also a matter of record that the order passed by the learned Assistant Commissioner is challenged in W.P.
No.34651/2016 and W.P. Nos.37109/2016.
In the wake of these facts, in my view, the allegations of forgery leveled against the petitioners necessarily require to be investigated into.

In the said circumstances in view of the prima NC:
2023:KHC:21390 facie allegations attracting the criminal offence, merely on the ground of pendency of the civil proceedings, the criminal process cannot be set at naught at the initial stage.
However, the allegation of forgery having been directed only against petitioner No.1, the action initiated against petitioner No.1 cannot be quashed.

10. Coming to the offences alleged against petitioners No.2 to 5 are concerned, I do not find any specific allegation in the entire complaint regarding the involvement of petitioners No.2 to 5 either in the fabrication of the document or in the forgery alleged to have been committed in the execution of the aforesaid Will.

These petitioners appear to have been implicated solely on the ground that they have Smt Savithramma vs State Of Karnataka on 20 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/177768181/
4 entered into an agreement to purchase the said properties from petitioner No.1.

entities.text: Smt Savithramma vs State Of Karnataka
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Needless to say that mere entering into an agreement in respect of the disputed properties does not amount to a criminal offence.
Moreover, this agreement has not fructified into any sale deed.

The learned counsel for respondent No.2 has also pointed out that the Will in question was not referred anywhere in the aforesaid agreement of sale which is indicative of the fact that petitioners No.2 to 5 were not in the knowledge of the execution or the existence of the said Will at the time of entering into said agreement.
Therefore, either way petitioners No.2 to 5 cannot be implicated in any of the above offences.

As a result, I do not have any hesitation to hold that the prosecution of petitioners No.2 to 5 for the alleged offences is wholly illegal, malafide, and baseless, and therefore,
cannot be continued.
To this extent, the petition deserves to be allowed.
Accordingly, the petition is allowed in part.
The petition filed on behalf of accused No.1 under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. is dismissed.
The investigation shall continue against accused No.1.
The petition filed on behalf of petitioners No.2 to 5 (accused Nos.2 to 5 in Crime No.520 of 2016) is allowed.

The proceedings in P.C.R. No.8250 of 2016 and Crime No.520 of 2016 on the file of V Additional NC: 2023:KHC:21390 CMM, Bengaluru, is quashed only insofar as petitioners No.2 to 5 (accused Nos.2 to 5) are concerned.

It is made clear that during the course of investigation if any incriminating evidence surfaces in proof the involvement of petitioners No.2 to 5 in any of the above offences, the Investigating Agency as well as the Court is at liberty to proceed against petitioners No.2 to 5 (accused Nos.2 to 5) in accordance with law."
(Emphasis supplied)
The co-ordinate Bench quashes the proceedings against accused Nos.2 to 5.
Insofar as the petitioner is concerned, it was directed that investigation would be necessary.

The co- ordinate Bench clearly observes that the allegation of forgery is directed only against petitioner No.1 i.e., the petitioner in the subject petition and the action initiated against the first petitioner cannot be quashed merely on the ground of civil proceedings between the parties is pending before the concerned Court.
The said order has become final as the petitioner has not challenged it before any higher fora.
Therefore, the petitioner cannot now contend that the private complaint is not sworn to by an affidavit.

Having suffered an order with regard to the allegations of forgery, which is staring at the petitioner, cannot now turn around and contend that the - 10 - NC: 2023:KHC:21390 proceedings are civil in nature or the complaint did not accompany an affidavit or otherwise.
10.

After the order being passed by the co-ordinate Bench of this Court, investigation continues against the petitioner and the police after investigation have filed a charge sheet before the concerned Court.

The summary of the charge sheet at column No.7 reads as follows:

A perusal at the order passed by the co-ordinate Bench as also the summary of the charge sheet supra, what would unmistakably emerge is that, the allegation of forgery point at the petitioner.
They both point at the petitioner at the stage of - 11 - NC: 2023:KHC:21390 registration of the crime and also in the summary of the charge sheet.

sentences.text: This is what is recorded by the co-ordinate Bench and permitted the investigation against the petitioner to continue.
It is for the aforesaid reasons, the petitioner has to come out clean in a trial.
11. The submission of the learned counsel for the petitioner that the issue is civil in nature does not merit acceptance as the co-ordinate Bench has rejected the same in Crl.P.No.6464/202016.
Even otherwise, it is no law, that merely because the issue is civil in nature, criminal proceedings should be quashed, to be of universal application to all the cases.
The applicability of such law depends on case to case basis.

12. The petitioner having suffered an order and the order becoming final, the filing of the charge sheet against the petitioner would all be factors that would run against the entertainment of the subject petition, inter alia.
